To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the next generation of the IASI instrument, with a spectral resolution of 1.5 cm−1, will be able to monitor lower troposphere ozone at a better vertical sensitivity and at a higher spatial and temporal resolution than IASI.

the next generation of instruments of the IASI type, with an instrumental configuration similar to that of IASI/2 described in this paper, will bring significant improvements in the monitoring of tropospheric (and especially lower tropospheric) ozone.
IASI-NG will bring a clear improvement of the quality of the LT ozone information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of the next generation IASI instrument, IASI-NG, for the monitoring of tropospheric air quality.
the potential of the next generation IASI instruments to better observe the ozone distribution in the troposphere and the associated error characteristics.
a possible scenario of a new generation of IASI-like instruments and the results are expected to be relevant for the design of IASI-NG and for other instruments of the same class.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IASI/2 will be able to monitor LT ozone at a higher accuracy, at a lower altitude and with a finer vertical resolution, with respect to the IASI instrument, thus providing a better monitoring of LT ozone and its variability.

the next generation of infrared sounders, such as IASI-NG, is expected to provide an improved monitoring of ozone in the lower troposphere, with a better spatial, temporal and vertical resolution, with respect to the current generation of infrared sounder instruments.
the IASI/2 configuration is expected to be a very powerful instrument to monitor ozone, with an improvement in the monitoring of LT ozone of a factor 3 to 4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IASI/2 has the potential to improve significantly the current capability of IASI to monitor LT ozone, thus providing a valuable tool for air quality monitoring and climate studies.
IASI/2 will bring a significant added value with respect of IASI to monitor lower troposphere ozone, in terms of accuracy, vertical and temporal resolution, and sensitivity at low altitude.
IASI/2 would provide an improvement in LT ozone monitoring, especially in terms of vertical resolution, vertical sensitivity, and sensitivity at lower altitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IASI/2 could bring a significant improvement of the monitoring of LT ozone.

, if the IASI/2 instrumental configuration can be implemented, the expected improvements in terms of sensitivity and vertical resolution will bring a clear benefit in terms of ozone monitoring, especially for lower tropospheric layers, and for the monitoring of ozone patterns at local scale.

IASI/2 could be an important tool to better understand the processes that govern the ozone distribution in the troposphere and to improve our knowledge of ozone chemistry and transport in the troposphere.
